title: Transformation of Bacillus subtilis with DNA obtained from natural donor cell lysis
author: James P. Finn IV

steps_raw.title: Two days before the transformation: Preparing donor and recipient strains.
steps_raw.instruction: Streak out the donor strain onto a LB agar plate with appropriate antibiotics and incubate at 37 °C for approximately 18 hours to obtain fresh, single colonies.

steps_raw.title: Two days before the transformation: Preparing donor and recipient strains.
steps_raw.instruction: Streak out the recipient strain onto a LB agar plate and incubate at 30 °C for, at most, 42 hours to obtain fresh, single colonies in two days.

steps_raw.title: One day before the transformation: Preparing the donor culture.
steps_raw.instruction: If the recipient was not streaked out yesterday, then streak out the recipient onto a LB agar plate with appropriate antibiotics and incubate at 37 °C for fresh, single colonies about 18 hours later.

steps_raw.title: One day before the transformation: Preparing the donor culture.
steps_raw.instruction: In 18mm sterile, glass test tubes, prepare 1 mL, 1x MC medium for each donor .

steps_raw.title: One day before the transformation: Preparing the donor culture.
steps_raw.instruction: Inoculate 1 mL, 1x MC medium with one donor colony.

steps_raw.title: One day before the transformation: Preparing the donor culture.
steps_raw.instruction: Alternatively, standard 96-well plates may be used with 200 µL of 1x MC medium per well or square deep-well, 96-well plates may be used with 400 µL of 1x MC medium per well. Note: ensure there is enough donor culture for the number of unique transformations.

steps_raw.title: One day before the transformation: Preparing the donor culture.
steps_raw.instruction: Table for making 1 mL or 400 µL of 1x MC medium. A B 1 900 µL sterile ddH2O 360 µL sterile ddH2O 2 3 µL 1M MgSO4 1.2 µL 1M MgSO4 3 100 µL 10x MC (stored at -30°C) 40 µL 10x MC (stored at -30°C) 4 1 mL of 1x MC 400 µL of 1x MC Column A is for 1 mL of 1x MC medium. Column B is for 400 µL of 1x MC medium.

steps_raw.title: One day before the transformation: Preparing the donor culture.
steps_raw.instruction: Vortex at setting 3 to 4 for 10 seconds and remove the inoculating stick. 00:00:10, Vortex

steps_raw.title: One day before the transformation: Preparing the donor culture.
steps_raw.instruction: Alternatively, if using 96-well plates, then use a pipette tip to inoculate each well with a colony.

steps_raw.title: One day before the transformation: Preparing the donor culture.
steps_raw.instruction: Incubate donor culture at 37 °C with aeration. Note: 18 mm test tubes can aerate rolling in a roller drum. Note: 96-well plates should have an aeration seal applied and aerate on a platform shaker at 350 rpm.

steps_raw.title: One day before the transformation: Preparing the donor culture.
steps_raw.instruction: Incubate for 20-24 hours to obtain sufficient cell lysis. 24:00:00, Donor Incubation

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Four hours before the end of the 20-24 hours incubation time for the donor, prepare 1 mL, 1x MC medium for the recipient in sterile, 18mm glass test tubes.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Inoculate 1 mL, 1x MC medium with one recipient colony using a sterile inoculation stick.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Incubate the recipient cultures at 37 °C for 4 hours with aeration. Use the same aeration methods as used for the donor cultures. go to step #7 04:00:00, Recipient Incubation

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Shortly before 4 hours have elapsed, prepare the donor for transformation: Is it necessary to filter the donor? (see Before Start)

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Donor DNA source may sit at room temperature while preparing the transformation tubes, but it can be stored at -30 °C .

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: The recipient can be grown in either glass test tubes or 96-well plates: Will the recipient be grown in Test Tubes or 96-well plates? (Select from the first step case below and continue within that step case for the remainder of the protocol.)

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Incubate the recipient cultures at 37 °C for 4 hours with aeration. Use the same aeration methods as used for the donor cultures. go to step #7 04:00:00, Recipient Incubation

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: If filtration is necessary (see Before Start):

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: If working in 18 mm glass test tubes:

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Aliquot 1 mL sample of the donor to a 1.7-microfuge tube.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Spin the sample at 21,000 x g in a centrifuge for 1 minute. Remove supernatant to a new microfuge tube. Take care not to disrupt cells and cell debris in pellet.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Filter the supernatant through a 0.22 µm PES filter. This filtrate is the source of donor DNA. Note: cellulose acetate and nylon filters are equally effective, but PES is usually most cost effective.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Donor DNA source may sit at room temperature while preparing the transformation tubes.
Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Is the donor growing in test tube or 96-well plate format?

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Filter away from the donor bacteria with a 0.22 µm filter type. This filtrate is the source of donor DNA.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Donor DNA source may sit at room temperature while preparing the transformation tubes, but it can be stored at -30 °C .

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Aliquot 1 mL sample of the donor to a 1.7-microfuge tube.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Spin the sample at 21,000 x g (max speed) in a centrifuge for 1 minute. 21000 x g, °C, 1 minute, Spin the donor sample

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Remove supernatant to a new microfuge tube. Take care not to disrupt cells and cell debris in pellet.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Filter the supernatant through a 0.22 µm PES filter. This filtrate is the source of donor DNA. Note: cellulose acetate and nylon filters are equally effective, but PES is usually most cost effective.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Inoculate each well of a 96-well plate with 200 µL, 1x MC medium with recipient . Note: A deep-well, 96-well plate can be used for the recipient growth with 400 µL of 1x MC medium.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: If using one recipient , then inoculate each well with 200 µL of 1x MC medium with recipient .

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: If using many unique recipients , then use a pipette tip to inoculate each well with one colony.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Shortly before 4 hours have elapsed, prepare the donor for transformation: Is it necessary to filter the donor? (see Before Start)

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Is the donor growing in test tube or 96-well plate format?

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Aliquot 1 mL sample of the donor to a 1.7-microfuge tube.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Spin the sample at 21,000 x g (max speed) in a centrifuge for 1 minute. 21000 x g, °C, 1 minute, Spin the donor sample

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Remove supernatant to a new microfuge tube. Take care not to disrupt cells and cell debris in pellet.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Filter the supernatant through a 0.22 µm PES filter. This filtrate is the source of donor DNA. Note: cellulose acetate and nylon filters are equally effective, but PES is usually most cost effective.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Donor DNA source may sit at room temperature while preparing the transformation tubes, but it can be stored at -30 °C .

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Aspirate directly from the donor culture and use this as the source of donor DNA . Note: This aspiration of the donor can happen from either a test tubes or a 96-well plate. Note: Due to the selective pressure, no spin is necessary.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Filter away from the donor bacteria with a 0.22 µm filter type. This filtrate is the source of donor DNA.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Donor DNA source may sit at room temperature while preparing the transformation tubes, but it can be stored at -30 °C .

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Transfer 200 µL of the recipient to a sterile, 13mm glass tube (this is the transformation tube).

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Transfer 10 µL of donor filtrate to the transformation tube.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Transfer 200 µL of the recipient to a sterile, 13mm glass tube (this is the transformation tube).

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Transfer 10 µL of donor lysate to the transformation tube.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Is the donor growing in test tube or 96-well plate format?

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Aspirate directly from the donor culture and use this as the source of donor DNA . Note: This aspiration of the donor can happen from either a test tubes or a 96-well plate. Note: Due to the selective pressure, no spin is necessary.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Transfer 200 µL of the recipient to a fresh well of a 96-well plate.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Transfer 10 µL of donor lysate to the transformation well.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Transfer 200 µL of the recipient to a fresh well of a 96-well plate.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Transfer 10 µL of donor filtrate to the transformation well.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Place transformations at 37 °C for 2 hours with aeration. Use the same aeration methods as used for the donor cultures. go to step #7 02:00:00, Transformation Growth

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Dilute transformation cultures 1:10 and 1:100.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Use 4-5 beads per petri plate to spread the cells evenly. Note: do not allow the liquid to sit on the agar plate for too long before spreading.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Incubate plates at 37 °C overnight, 30 °C for two days, or Room temperature for three days. Note: the resulting colonies should be the desired transformants.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Dispense 100 µL to 200 µL on appropriate selective plates. Note: ensure the agar plates are not so dry that they prevent even spreading.

steps_raw.title: Day of the transformation: Mixing donor and recipient.
steps_raw.instruction: Place transformations at 37 °C for 2 hours with aeration. Use the same aeration methods as used for the donor cultures. go to step #7 Note: Use the large 18 mm tubes with small caps or 1 mL pipette tips inside to hold the small 13 mm glass tubes (See Figure 1 in Loyo & Burton 2018, link in References Section ). 02:00:00, Transformation Growth
